justification: B is set in a more legible serif with a clear sans heading hierarchy. Its abstract sits in a framed box, and its header and footer bands give navigation and page numbers. The chart is titled and coloured to match the scheme (B2, B4). A is a plain, competent LaTeX-style layout. It is denser, and its heavy black bars and small table caption feel cruder (A1, A3). B's mostly empty title page costs some space, and its references lose their [1]/[2] numbering (B5), so the margin is moderate.

The two designs share the same content and structure. A fits it into 5 pages, with each page fairly full. B runs to 6 pages, and its last page holds only a lone table, leaving most of B6 empty. A breaks the Arabic section across pages (A3–A4), but its page flow is tighter overall. B's serif body and numbered headings read slightly better, though not enough to outweigh the stranded table and the extra page.

A fits the content in 5 pages and avoids B's orphaned final table on B6, which sits alone on a mostly empty page. A's bold sans headings and blue KPI figures give clearer hierarchy than B's light serif headings on B3–B5. A has some flaws: headings hang outside the text column, and the Arabic is small and set in a single line with uneven wrapping (A5). B's Arabic is larger and more legible, and its running header and footer look polished. On balance, A's tighter flow and stronger section structure edge it ahead.

Both designs share the same layout. B's sans headings with a blue accent give clearer hierarchy, and its KPI figures stand out more (B2). On A6, the dark navy donut makes the dark percentage labels nearly invisible. On B6 the medium-blue fill keeps them legible. A's small serif captions on A4 and A6 also read weaker than B's.

A keeps one body size with numbered section headings throughout, which gives a steady reading rhythm. B enlarges the first paragraph after every heading into a lead paragraph. This makes the text size jump on every page. B also outdents its headings well past the text column, which leaves a ragged left edge. B splits a Results paragraph across pages 3 and 4. A's heavy navy header and footer bands are somewhat heavy, but they stay consistent. B's lighter footers and rules are cleaner, yet they do not outweigh its uneven type.

A has bolder Montserrat-style section heads, readable serif body text and a lead paragraph, but it spends a whole cover page on the title with nothing else. Its headings hang outdented past the text column, and the large lead paragraphs make the text sizes uneven. B opens with a compact title band that leads straight into the abstract and keeps one consistent text measure. Its running header and footer bands give a steady four-page rhythm. B's light headings are weaker than A's, but the layout overall is tighter and more consistent.

A spreads thin content over 8 pages, leaving large empty areas. The abstract sits alone on A2, and the chart is stranded on A6 with a mostly blank page. Lead paragraphs are set larger, which reads as inconsistent sizing. B flows compactly over 4 pages with even density. It places the table and chart together with the results on B3, and its banded header and footer are consistent. A's serif text is pleasant, but its pacing and balance are poor.

B is the more coherent academic layout. It has a compact abstract with inline labels, numbered bold section heads, and a captioned figure and table. Its references are numbered to match the in-text [1] [2] citations. A has a strong navy title band and header and footer bands. However, its abstract splits each label from its sentence, which wastes space. Its light section heads are weak against the body text. Its running headers show the wrong section, for example 'Discussion' on a page that is mostly Results and 'Methods' on a page that also holds Results. B leaves a large gap at the bottom of page 2, but overall it reads more cleanly.

A frames every page with dark header and footer bands and sets its headings consistently, but it spills a lone table onto A6, leaving a mostly empty final page. B fits the content into five pages with fuller, more even pages (B4, B5). Its bold headings hold up well. Its weaknesses are the misaligned indented English body text and a broken Arabic line on B5. On balance, B's tighter pagination wins slightly.

The two designs share the same structure and pagination, including the orphaned table on the last page. A pairs an elegant serif with a well-sized, justified Arabic face, and its Arabic body text sits comfortably beside the Latin. B uses a heavier slab serif with loose justified English lines that show visible word gaps. B's Arabic body is smaller and lighter, and its running headers add clutter. A reads more refined overall.

A pairs a serif Latin face with Arabic and keeps each Arabic section whole on its page; its Arabic text is set larger and reads better. B uses five pages against A's six, and its header and footer bands are stronger. However, B splits the Performance Highlights Arabic paragraph across B3–B4, which breaks reading flow. B's Arabic body is also small and cramped. A's main flaw is the orphaned table on A6, but its sections read more coherently on A3–A5.

A sets Arabic text at a comfortable size matching the Latin, with consistent alignment and a calm serif heading system. B's Arabic body and labels are noticeably tiny and cramped. Its English body is indented inconsistently with headings, and B5 shows a broken bidi wrap leaving "4.2bn)." orphaned on its own line. A does spill a lone table onto A6, but its pages read more cleanly overall.

B pairs serif body text with bold numbered sans headings, which gives clearer hierarchy and more comfortable long-form reading. A uses light-weight thin sans headings, and its body text runs dense to the bottom of every page. B's cover page is sparse, but its section breaks breathe better and the figure is given more room. A's banded title header is attractive, but its light text weight weakens hierarchy.

The two designs share the same content and flow, including the orphaned table on page 6. A pairs a sans display face with serif body text, giving crisper KPI numbers. Its heavy navy header and footer bands frame the pages strongly but feel heavy, and they carry tiny text. B uses a consistent serif with light hairline header and footer rules, which feels calmer and more refined. A's numbered headings add slight clarity, but they also create oddities like the Arabic headings numbered '2' and '4'. Overall B is marginally more polished.

A has a refined serif with rule-separated sections, but its Scope of Work list breaks across pages, leaving 'b. Consent service' orphaned at the top of A2. B keeps the full list together on B1, so B2 starts cleanly with the timeline. B also uses numbered bold headings and a running header and footer. B's hyphenated 'Decem-ber' is a small flaw, but the broken list in A is worse.

B packs content tighter and adds running header/footer bands, but its pie and donut charts are scaled up so their labels balloon and get clipped: "26.6%" runs into "West" and "6.1%" is cut off on B3. On the donut in B4 the percentage labels are illegible. Its squashed bar, line and area charts on B2–B4 also lose detail. A gives each chart proper proportions with readable labels (A3–A6) and a clean KPI hierarchy on A2, though it leaves more empty space.

Design B sets its Arabic text larger and more legibly, while Design A's Arabic is small and cramped (A3, A4). B adds header and footer bands with running titles and page numbers (B2–B6). B also aligns its headings to the margin, whereas A's English headings hang outside the text column, which looks inconsistent (A3). B's drawback is an extra page holding only one table (B6). A has narrower spacing, and one Arabic paragraph wraps "SAR 4.2bn" across lines (A5).

A spreads thin content over 8 pages. The abstract page and the chart page are mostly empty (A2, A6), and the chart is separated from its table (A5–A6). A sets the first paragraph of each section in a larger lead size, which reads as inconsistent. A's references lack numbering, so the [1] and [2] citations don't link up. B is a compact 4-page academic layout with numbered headings and the table and captioned figure grouped together (B3). B also numbers its references and keeps a steady paragraph rhythm. A has an attractive dark cover, but its balance is poor overall.

A gives each chart room at consistent scale with clean serif type and a calm KPI block. B crams charts onto pages and squashes them (B2 bar and line, B4 area). Its pie and donut are oversized, with clipped labels ('26.6', '6.1%') and huge mismatched label fonts on B3 and B4. The donut percentages in both are barely legible. B's header and footer bands are tidy but don't make up for the distorted imagery. A's summary page leaves a lot of empty space (A2).

A keeps the Scope of Work list whole on page 1 and uses bold, numbered sans headings that stand out clearly from the serif body. B's light headings are weaker and lean on rule dividers. B also splits the scope list across pages, leaving 'b. Consent service' orphaned at the top of B2. A has a hyphenated 'Decem-ber' break, but that flaw is minor.

B's bold numbered headings and serif body text give clearer hierarchy and steadier reading. A's light-weight headings with rule lines feel weaker and repetitive. A's dark header bar on page 2 is a nice touch. However, B hyphenates 'Decem-ber' awkwardly, so the margin is small.

Both designs share the same structure, including the orphaned table on page 6. B's serif type with a matching Arabic face reads more cohesively. Its thin top rule and quiet footer are less heavy than A's dark full-width header and footer bands, which repeat running heads on every page. A's numbered headings mix a sans font with serif body text, and its Arabic body text is set tighter. The differences are modest.

B keeps the Scope of Work list whole on page 1, while A splits item 3 onto page 2 as an orphan (A2). B also uses a consistent left alignment, with headings and body sharing one edge. A outdents its headings with hanging rules, which gives a ragged left margin and an off-centre feel (A1, A2). B has proper running headers and footers (B2). A's rules between sections add some structure, but they do not outweigh the orphaned list item.

A uses one consistent sans family with Arabic set at a comparable size, plus navy header/footer bands that frame each page. B mixes a serif body with a geometric sans and sets the Arabic text noticeably small. B's section headings and body also have awkward indents, and its rules run off-grid. B does have bolder section heads, but A reads more cohesively.

A uses an oversized lead paragraph after each heading and hangs its headings outdented into the left margin, which makes the body column look inconsistent and ragged (A2–A5). B keeps one consistent text size and a single aligned column throughout (B2–B5). B also adds numbered headings and header/footer bands that aid navigation. Its heavy dark bands are a little strong, but the overall text is steadier and more even.

Both share the same structure and the orphaned table on the last page. A's refined serif with matched Arabic face reads more elegantly, and its thin top rule with a quiet footer stays out of the way. B's heavy dark header and footer bands and numbered headings add clutter. B's justified Latin text also shows wider word gaps.

A packs two charts per page but its pie and donut on A3–A4 render with oversized labels, a giant 'Figure 3' title and clipped percentages (26.6%, 6.1%), which looks broken. B gives each chart its own page with properly scaled labels and figure titles (B4, B7). It leaves large empty lower halves on B3–B6 and runs to more pages. B's numbered serif body also reads more cleanly.

A pairs a bold sans heading face with serif body text, so section headings (Executive Summary, Objectives, Investment) stand out strongly and the page is easy to scan. B sets its headings in a light serif at a weight close to the body text, which weakens the hierarchy. A's blue cover band is more vivid. B's alignment is consistent. Its list split leaves an orphaned "b. Consent service" at the top of page 2, while A splits more cleanly after item 2. A has a small hyphenation break, "Decem-ber", in Next Steps. The tables are near identical in both designs.

A fits the content into five well-filled pages. Its navy header and footer bands carry running titles, and its page flow is consistent. B spills onto a sixth page that holds only an orphaned table (B6), which leaves a mostly empty page. B's serif typography is elegant, but its thin top rule and sparse footers give weaker structure. A splits an Arabic paragraph across pages (A3–A4), but B's orphaned table is the bigger flaw.

A gives each chart consistent scaling with clean, proportionate labels. B packs charts at inconsistent sizes: the pie on B3 and the donut on B4 have oversized labels, and the pie's percentage labels are clipped ('6.1%', '26.6'). Figures 1, 2 and 5 are squashed flat. A leaves a lot of empty space on each page, but its consistent rhythm and legible figures outweigh B's compactness.

A runs to six pages, and its last page holds only an orphaned table with a mostly empty page below it (A6). B fits the same content into five pages. B's dark navy header and footer bands give a stronger frame (B2–B5). B has flaws too: the Arabic paragraph splits across pages B3 and B4, its sans text is slightly lighter and less readable, and the pages are dense. A's serif type and generous space read comfortably (A3, A4), but the trailing near-blank page weighs against it.

A runs as a compact, consistent document: a navy title band, an abstract on page one, running header and footer bands, and evenly set body text in a single sans family. B spends its whole first page on a mostly empty cover. Its section headings hang out into the left margin, misaligned with the indented body. Each section's first paragraph is set in a larger lead style, which breaks the text rhythm. B's serif body text is pleasant, but its overall structure is less coherent than A's.

A pairs serif body text with bold numbered headings, so sections stand out clearly and long passages read comfortably. Its cover page is sparse but clean. B's dark title band is striking and saves a page. However, its light-weight sans body and thin, light headings make the hierarchy weaker. Its narrow condensed text is also harder to read over long stretches.

A runs the content continuously across 4 pages, with consistent bands and the chart placed right after its table. B spreads the same content over 8 pages. Its abstract sits alone on a mostly empty page, the chart is stranded on its own page, and pages 3–5 have large empty bottoms. Each section in B also opens with an inconsistent enlarged lead paragraph that breaks the rhythm.

A's pie and donut charts render with oversized labels and clipped percentages: '6.1%' and '26.6' are cut off on A3, and the donut values are illegible on A4. A's charts are also squashed. B renders the same charts cleanly with proportional labels and gives each figure room (B4, B6). A's dark header and footer bands and boxed summary are polished, but B's large revenue KPI and serif body text read well. B does leave a large empty area on B2.

A is a compact four-page paper. The table and chart sit together with their text on A3, and the section flow is even. B spreads the same content over eight pages. The abstract is stranded on a mostly empty page (B2), and every section is forced onto a new page, leaving half-blank pages (B3, B4). The chart sits alone on B6, cut off from its table on B5. The equation font in B4 also clashes with the body text. B's cover and rules look polished, but the pacing is wasteful and fragmented.

A forces page breaks after every section, so A2, A3, A4 and A6 are left mostly empty. The chart sits alone on A6, and A8 holds only two orphan lines. B flows its sections continuously and places the chart directly under its table on B4. Its bold sans headings stand out clearly against the serif body. A's dark cover is striking, but B's pages read as a compact, balanced document.

A keeps the Scope of Work list intact on page 1, while B splits its final item "3. Activation and training" onto the top of page 2, leaving a stranded orphan. B also hyphenates "Decem-ber" in a short closing line. A adds a running header band and a footer, which makes page 2 feel finished. B's bolder headings give stronger contrast, but its outdented heads and ragged indent feel less consistent.

Design A keeps a single consistent left edge, so headings, text and tables align cleanly, and its serif headings feel unified and restrained. Design B hangs bold sans headings outside the text column while the rules end short on the right, which makes the layout feel uneven. B also has awkward hyphenation ('e-commerce' split across lines, 'Decem-ber' on B2), and its saturated blue band is less refined than A's navy one. B's bolder headings do scan faster, but A is more polished overall.

Design A sets each chart alone on its page, leaving the bottom half of A3, A5 and A6 empty. Its donut labels on A7 are dark on navy and barely legible. Design B pairs charts two to a page on B3 and B5, which gives fuller, steadier pages, and its donut percentages on B6 are readable. B's summary page (B2) has a weak empty lower half, while A's KPI row with the chart on A2 is tidier, and A's header bands add structure. On balance B reads better.

A pairs bold numbered sans headings with a serif body, giving clear section hierarchy and comfortable reading. B uses light, unnumbered headings that sit weakly under the rule lines. B also sets everything in one condensed sans, so body text is denser and less distinct. The tables and cover bands are comparable. B's dark header band on page 2 is a nice touch but does not offset A's stronger headings.

A packs content into 5 well-filled pages: the abstract shares a page with the introduction, and the table and chart sit together with their text. B spreads the same content over 8 sparse pages. Its abstract stands alone on B2, and its chart is orphaned on a mostly empty B6. Large blank areas recur on B3, B4 and B8. B's small, light body text and its oversized lead paragraphs make the rhythm uneven. B's dark cover is striking, but it doesn't make up for this.

Both share the same layout and the same page-6 table orphan. A's serif body text is larger and more legible, and its green accent rules and running headers give clearer section context. B uses smaller, lighter English text, and its tables are faint with small type (B3, B4). The heavy Arabic face in B looks mismatched beside its light English serif. A's text and tables read more comfortably (A3, A4).

A has a polished cover, branded headings and coloured chart, but its body is inconsistent: every lead paragraph switches to a larger size with a ragged margin, and the headings hang outside the text column. It also misses things a reader relies on. The references are unnumbered although the text cites [1] and [2]. The abstract box is cramped, with labels stacked above one-line entries. B is a plain LaTeX-style article with a uniform justified body and numbered sections. Its abstract is compact, the figure has a proper caption, and the references are numbered. B reads more cleanly and consistently.

Design B packs the same content into five pages and avoids A's near-empty final page, where a lone table sits orphaned at the top of A6. B's pages are fuller and more evenly filled (B3–B5). It does split an Arabic paragraph across B3 and B4, but that is a lesser flaw. A keeps sections whole and has slightly calmer spacing on A3 and A4. Its serif and sans pairing is comparable to B's single sans, and the tables are equivalent in both.

A is a plain but well-ordered academic layout. Its bold numbered headings are clear, the figure has a caption, and the references are numbered. B has a polished navy title band, a boxed abstract, running headers and footers, and a coloured chart, so it looks more finished. However, B's section headings are light-weight, and its abstract labels sit on separate lines, wasting space. B's running header also mislabels sections (B3 shows 'Discussion' while Results is still on the page), and its references lost their [1]/[2] numbering (B4). Overall B's visual finish slightly outweighs these flaws for most readers.

A keeps the full Scope of Work list on page 1. B splits it mid-list, stranding 'b. Consent service' and item 3 at the top of B2. A also adds a running header band with the section name and 'Page 2 of 2' on page 2. B's serif styling is elegant, and its stats are aligned the same way, but the broken list hurts its continuity. A's heavier sans title gives a stronger cover hierarchy.

Both designs share the same layout. A pairs a bold sans heading with serif body, which gives clearer heading contrast; B's all-serif headings are weaker at small sizes (B4, B6). B's very dark navy fill makes the dark donut percentage labels nearly invisible (B6), while A keeps them faintly legible (A6). B's top rule and full-title running footer are minor pluses but do not offset this. A's mid-blue charts read more easily.

A uses consistent serif typography with full running headers and footers, and its section rules and body text stay within one aligned measure. B's body text is indented while its rules overrun the right margin (B3–B5). On B5 the Arabic bidi wraps badly, splitting 'SAR 4.2bn' across lines. B's KPI figures also crowd one another. A's flaw is a nearly empty orphan table page (A6), which hurts its rhythm. B fits the content into five pages, but its alignment and text defects are more noticeable.

A pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, so section headings stand out clearly and the text reads with warmth. B uses light-weight headings that barely outrank its thin body text, which flattens the hierarchy. B keeps the Scope list whole on page 1 and adds a running header. A splits item 3 onto page 2 and leaves an orphan line there. B's headings are weak enough that A still reads better overall.

B has the stronger hierarchy. Its sans headings sit under rule lines, it has running footers and a boxed abstract (B2), and it uses a tinted table and chart with a clear title (B4). It does have flaws. The cover page is mostly empty (B1). Each section's lead paragraph is set larger, so text size jumps oddly (B2, B3, B5). The References heading is cramped against the Limitations text (B5). A is a plain, consistent Times layout that reads evenly, but it is flat. Its heavy black bars and a table caption jammed against the text above (A3) make it less polished overall.

B pairs its charts two per page (B3, B5), which avoids A's run of pages that each hold one half-page chart above large empty areas (A3, A5, A6). B's KPI hero on B2 is striking, though the rest of that page is left empty. A has stronger numbered headings and solid header and footer bands (A2), but its sparse pagination weighs more against it. Both donut charts have low-contrast labels (A7, B6).

Both designs share the same layout and content flow, including the orphaned table on page 6. A uses a coherent serif family with a matching Arabic face and light, thin-ruled header and footer. B mixes a sans display face with serif body text, adds awkward numbering such as "2 كلمة" in the Arabic headings, and uses heavy dark header and footer bars that crowd the pages. A reads calmer and more consistent.

A forces a page break before every section, so pages are left mostly empty: A2 holds only the abstract, A3 is half empty, A6 has a lone chart over a blank page, and A8 carries just two widow lines plus the references. Its lead paragraphs set in larger type make for a nice opening, and its type is legible. B runs the content continuously across five pages with well-filled pages (B2–B5). It puts the table and chart together beside the results (B4), uses clear numbered headings, and adds running header and footer bands. B's centred title wraps awkwardly on B1, and its banding is heavier, but overall it reads far more evenly.

A splits the Scope of Work list across the page break, leaving 'b. Consent service' and '3. Activation and training' orphaned at the top of A2. B keeps the whole list on B1 and opens B2 cleanly with the Timeline section under a running header. A's loose list spacing helps fill page 1, but B's intact sections read better. Tables are comparable. B's hyphenated justified text is a minor drawback.

A pairs Montserrat headings with a serif body, which gives strong section heads. But its English sections hang out into the left margin, misaligned with the body text and rules (A3–A5), and its Arabic body is set small and cramped. B uses a consistent sans family with aligned margins. Its Arabic body is larger and more legible, and header and footer bands add page context and running titles (B2–B5). B's light-weight section heads are weaker, but its alignment and readability win overall.

Design A packs the content into five pages with steady fill. Its navy header and footer bands frame each page clearly. Design B's serif type reads well, but it ends with a nearly empty sixth page holding only one orphaned table (B6). B4 also leaves a large blank area at the bottom. Design A's Arabic paragraph splits across pages (A3 to A4), but its page rhythm and fill are more consistent overall.

A pairs related charts two to a page (A3, A5), so pages feel full and paced. B places one small chart per page and leaves large empty bottoms on B3, B5 and B6. B's donut percentage labels are nearly invisible against the dark fill (B7), while A's are readable (A6). B's header and footer bands and section numbering add structure, but A's hero KPI layout on A2 gives the stronger figure hierarchy.

A fits the content into 5 pages. Its pages are densely but consistently filled. Its bold sans headings stand out clearly against the serif body. B's light serif section heads are weaker. B also splits a KPI block and table away from the Operations section onto B5. Its final page, B6, holds only one orphaned table, leaving most of the page empty. B does gain from running headers and footers, but the awkward pagination outweighs that. A's outdented headings and rules give it a steadier rhythm.

A flows its sections continuously, with bold sans headings that set clear hierarchy, and it keeps the table and chart together on A4. B forces page breaks after every section, so pages are left mostly empty: the abstract alone on B2, the chart stranded on B6, and the references orphaned on B8. B's light serif headings are also weaker. B's dark cover is attractive, but it does not offset these pacing problems.

A keeps the Scope of Work list whole on page 1. B splits it, stranding item 3 at the top of B2. A also aligns its headings with the body text on a consistent left margin and numbers its sections. B hangs its headings in the outer margin with indented body text, so the page feels off-balance, and its saturated blue band looks harsher than A's navy. A's running header and footer are neater too.

A's pie chart on A3 is badly scaled, with an oversized 'Figure 3' title and labels clipped (6.1%, 26.6% cut off). Its donut on A4 also has oversized labels. A is more compact and its banded headers are tidy, but B renders the charts cleanly at consistent scale (B4, B6). B also gives each section breathing room. B2 leaves a lot of empty space, yet overall B reads more polished.

A pairs its charts two per page (A3, A5), so pages are evenly filled and the report reads steadily. B puts one chart on each page (B3, B5, B6), leaving the lower half of most pages blank. A's summary page (A2) is sparse but makes a bold KPI statement. B has stronger header and footer bands and a compact KPI row with numbered headings (B2). Both share the illegible donut labels.

A pairs a clean sans heading face with a serif body, sets the abstract in a boxed panel, and gives paragraphs generous spacing. Navy header and footer bands add running context. B is a plain Times-like layout with tight leading and denser pages. It does number its references and caption its figure properly, but it feels more cramped. A's near-empty cover page costs a page, yet overall A reads more comfortably.
